title: Natural Domain and Range of a Linear Radicand
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Find the natural domain and range of the function f(x) = \sqrt{4 - 2x}. Express your results in standard interval notation.
hints: Recall that an even-indexed radical requires its radicand to be non-negative in the real number system.
Set the expression under the square root 4 - 2x >= 0 and solve for x, remembering to reverse the inequality sign when dividing by a negative number.
For the range, observe the minimum value a principal square root can output and whether higher values are attainable.

steps.title: Formulate the Radicand Condition
steps.explanation: The square root function produces real values if and only if the expression inside is greater than or equal to zero.
steps.why: Negative numbers have imaginary square roots, which are outside the real number domain of single-variable calculus.

steps.title: Solve the Linear Inequality
steps.explanation: Subtract 4 from both sides and divide by -2, reversing the inequality sign from >= to <=.
steps.why: Multiplying or dividing both sides of an inequality by a negative number reverses the direction of the inequality.

steps.title: State the Natural Domain
steps.explanation: The domain contains all real numbers less than or equal to 2, inclusive of the boundary endpoint x = 2.
steps.why: The square root of zero is zero, which is a well-defined real number.

steps.title: Determine the Range
steps.explanation: The principal square root symbol denotes the non-negative root. As x decreases from 2 to -inf, 4 - 2x grows without bound, so sqrt(4 - 2x) covers all values in [0, inf).
steps.why: The principal square root function has a non-negative codomain [0, inf) and maps continuously to infinity.
